summary: The bill amends the Voting Rights Act of 1965 to restore and update preclearance by automatically covering states or localities with three or more voting rights violations in the prior 25 years and by requiring federal approval before implementing specific new practices such as at-large elections, certain redistricting, stricter voter ID rules, or reduced polling places in areas with significant minority populations.

The bill is a comprehensive amendment to the Voting Rights Act of 1965. It revises coverage formulas for preclearance, expands definitions of vote denial/dilution/abridgment, strengthens enforcement mechanisms (including observer assignments and Attorney General authority), adds transparency requirements for voting changes, and creates new preclearance triggers for covered practices. These changes are designed to expand voting access and strengthen protections against discriminatory election practices, directly advancing the -1 end of the spectrum.
